utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Before we proceed with the witness, the Trial Chamber has noticed that there is an application for a certificate by the Defence, and there is also an application for -- before the Appeals Chamber for leave to appeal, and there is also the decision of the duty Judge on the matter. So the Trial Chamber wants to know what the Defence has decided to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, and Happy New Year to all colleagues present here. The position of the Defence is that we don't have any particular interest to follow one or the other way. If this Trial Chamber will grant our application for a certificate, obviously it will be in the interest of the speediness of this trial and proceedings, which means that, in that case, we are not -- we shall not be in situation to wait for the decision of the bench of three Judges in Appeals Chamber, and then we could proceed with the appeal because this specific issue is, from our point of view, is very important, because we are facing certain limits and problems with regard to the testimony of today's present witness and the other witnesses with regard to the amendment of the indictment. So in short, we would prefer, based on our application, that this certificate will be given. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In that case, then, are you going to withdraw your application for leave to appeal?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is correct, because we shall appeal directly to the Appeals Chamber, in accordance with Rule 73, I suppose, (D).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think the matter does not appear to be clear, Mr. Pantelic, because if you look at 73(C) and (D), they are not alternatives to one issue. They are separate provisions. So if your decision is that you are going ahead with your application for a certificate, that is 73(C), and you are withdrawing the appeal, then you have to file the notice for withdrawal before the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, that would be a logical step. Of course, we are ready to file this notice, but you can understand this specific situation where we were obliged to act in a time limit of seven days. So in order not to -- not to go beyond this time limit, we decided to file both applications according to Rule 73 Sub-rule (C), which is a certificate, and also (D) Sub-rule (ii)(E).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But you appreciate that this appeal you're trying to get on is an interlocutory appeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is interlocutory appeal, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which, if you look at 73(C), interlocutory appeals are not allowed except if they fall under, as provision (C) provides, where you need the appeal decided if it concerns evidence of procedure and is appropriate for the continuation of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Our understanding is that the -- this particular situation is falling under the ambit of this Rule, because first of all, interlocutory appeal is allowed if the issue is related to general importance to proceeding before the Tribunal or International Court, which I would not say it's our case, but we are focusing to the general -- the issue of general importance to the proceedings before this Tribunal. And then we think that this certificate will allow us to file our appeal directly to Appeals Chamber, dealing with these particular issues, which are also related to procedure, because in Sub-rule (C) of Rule 73, we have -- we have practically twofold issues, which is the evidence or procedure, and we think that we are dealing with procedure here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. In that case, then, the Trial Chamber will wait for your withdrawal of the appeal, once you've filed the notice of withdrawal, and then we'll hear your submissions on your application for certificate under (C) and then we can make our decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, with all due respect, I think it would be, to some extent, dangerous for the Defence to withdraw our motion for leave to appeal and then to wait for your decision with regard to the certificate. For example, theoretically, if we shall not be in possession of the certificate and at the same time our application for leave to appeal will be withdrawn, then we shall be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But you see, Mr. Pantelic, (C) and (D) are different. The certificate is not intended to aid you to appeal. The certificate can only be granted under different circumstances from (D). Did you read the decision of the duty Judge?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour, but allow me to say that this -- that was the angle of view of duty Judge. Defence and all of my colleagues, we have the other approach to this issue. So that would be wise if we could clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. In that case, the Trial Chamber's view is you should file your notice of withdrawal under (D), and then we'll go ahead and deal with (C), 73(C). You'll make your submissions then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, I would kindly ask whichever this appropriate time for the conference, short conference with my colleague during the break this afternoon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- so we could inform Trial Chamber about our, I would say our final position with regard to this issue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we'll proceed with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. My mistake. If I -- if I could have a few more seconds. We are facing a rather specific situation now, because if I would understand, to the best of my knowledge, prior to the Christmas break, this witness was to give his evidence with regard to the issue which was introduced in the amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Our position is the following: Firstly, we have to inform this Trial Chamber that our clients are not in possession of the fourth amended indictment in their language, their native language, B/C/S, which means that that could be a certain obstacle for the further proceedings. Secondly, we are of the opinion that this specific issue with regard to the topics introduced in the -- in the fourth amended indictment are of significant importance for the -- for this trial in general. We think -- and therefore for this reason we filed our motion for leave to appeal. We think that the Prosecution should not be allowed to amend indictment with this particular -- with these particular charges, allegations, of course, because the Prosecution was in possession of all relevant statements and evidences --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you're trying to make your submissions as if we are hearing the appeal. Those are submissions before the Appeals Chamber if you elect to go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but since we don't have any final answer and response from the Appeals Chamber, we think that it would not be appropriate now to hear this portion of witness testimony related to the allegations -- related to allegations for destruction of the religious institution and so on. And I think that that would be our first, first part of our submission with regard to the -- to this particular issue, and my learned colleagues are in situation to give you additional information which might facilitate these proceedings, if you allow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Who is going to make submissions? Yes, Ms. Baen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is becoming confusing because we're trying not to create any problem that displeases the Trial Chamber, and the confusion came in where the motion for interlocutory appeal was filed and 73(C) and (D) were confused because we were trying to not create a huge problem. The position of the Defence is that we don't feel that this trial can continue until this panel that the President appointed gives us an answer on the issue that we filed for -- for which we filed for interlocutory appeal. Rule 73(D) uses a language and issues appropriate for interlocutory appeal if it would cause -- the decision would cause prejudice to the Defence that can't be cured by the final disposal of the trial, including post judgement appeal. The whole point, Your Honour, is we feel like the safer thing to do is to wait until this three-Judge panel makes a decision on this issue, and that would be the safer route to take instead of if we continue to go through the trial and this witness starts testifying about the evidence with respect to destruction of religious property, we get to the end of the trial, and at that point, after -- if the defendants are convicted, at that point the Appeals Chamber says, "Whoa, the Defence may have had a point there. Maybe they should have had some time to address this issue." I think the safer position is to give this three-Judge panel time to answer the issue instead of wait until the end of the trial and waste all the time in the trial, possibly. And I will tell you this also: My co-counsel told me - and I haven't discussed this with the other Defence counsel - but he told me that our investigators have not had adequate time to investigate the new -- these new allegations. They're new to us. I will just tell you that they haven't been investigated by our investigators. The allegations that are mentioned in the fourth amended indictment, about the destruction of religious property, there's a new date that was mentioned and we just got that information on January 9 of this year. The time frame when these crimes were allegedly committed were from September 1991 to December 31st, 1993. We just found this information out on January 9th. Therefore, we haven't had adequate time to address this -- these allegations. We're not prepared. And that's all we're saying, is the safer route would be for the Appeals Chamber to answer -- or this panel to answer the question about this issue and then we continue after that decision's been made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. That confuses the earlier submission by the Defence. So are you withdrawing your application for the certificate?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I will tell you -- on behalf of our clients, we're not withdrawing the interlocutory appeal. I haven't discussed with our client about the certificate because we were waiting to see what the Trial Chamber was going to tell us this afternoon. But at least on behalf of our client, we're not withdrawing the application for interlocutory appeal because that's a huge gamble because then, if Your Honours don't certify the issue, we've lost our right to argue under Rule 73(E).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But we don't seem to be getting anywhere. You are now standing up on behalf of your client, you are now saying you won't withdraw your application for leave to appeal, we go ahead with the certificate.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: All I'm saying, Your Honour, is on behalf of my client, and I don't know if I speak for the others, we feel that we have to have a stay in the proceedings until this three-Judge panel says whatever it's going to say on this issue that we raised. That's it. And we feel like it's dangerous for the trial to continue. If this evidence comes in on this destruction of religious institutions and then at the end of the trial the Appeals Chamber said, "Whoa, maybe that shouldn't have come in, then all this time is potentially wasted when the safer position is to let them answer the question. It may take two days. That's a lot better than wasting years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I'm just wondering why therefore no one from the Defence made any objections when the Prosecution was showing earlier witnesses the photographs in the bundle. I forget what the Prosecution evidence number is, but we saw those photographs of what appear to be just two grass plots one, one where the mosque was and one where the Catholic church was. There was no objection posed then. Likewise, with at least two of the earlier witnesses, we heard about the issue of -- I believe it was the mosque in Odzak being blown up. There was some controversy, I think, as to who actually did the blowing up, but again, those issues were raised then and there was -- there was no objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll tell you exactly why, Your Honour. First of all, they weren't allegations in the indictment. There's been a lot of information, a lot of testimony coming from these witnesses that has not been tied to these defendants as crimes, and I guess we could have objected and say it's not relevant because it's not in the indictment, but this isn't a jury trial. We've got three sophisticated Judges here; you decide what's relevant and what's not relevant. And it wasn't an allegation in the indictment so we didn't feel that they were pointing the finger at us and saying, "These guys are responsible for destruction of those mosques," because that was never said, and that's why we didn't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: May I get it clear. So for the Defence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Defence for Mr. Milan Simic, do I take it you would like to go ahead with your submission on the certificate?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might discuss this with my co-counsel. We have not discussed this yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On behalf of all the Defence counsel, we withdraw our request under Rule 73(C) for the certificate from the Trial Chamber, but we are not going to withdraw our interlocutory appeal application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So may I have confirmation that's the position, the application for the certificate under Rule 73(C) is withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, on behalf of Mr. Blagoje Simic too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on behalf of the Defence of Mr. Miroslav Tadic, we join the request of Mr. Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On behalf of the Simo Zaric Defence, we support the position of Milan Simic Defence and this is also our position in the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. So the -- so the request for a certificate based on Rule 73(C) filed on December 26, 2001 is hereby withdrawn by all the defendants.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I thought my mike was on. The request for a certificate based on Rule 73(C) on behalf of all the defendants is hereby withdrawn. There is no stay of proceedings, and the proceedings will continue. Yes. The Prosecution can go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. If Your Honours please, I take it, then, you don't wish to hear from the Prosecution on the issue raised by Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one? MR. DI FAZIO: Namely whether or not this evidence should simply be held over until the appeal is disposed of. The position of the Prosecution, of course, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution can make submissions, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- that you are professional Judges, sitting without a jury, and that you are quite capable, therefore, of excluding from your consideration evidence of damage or destruction of places of worship should it eventuate that the Appeals Chamber decides that it should not have been admitted, and that is the position of the Prosecution on that particular topic. [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the very least, we're requesting -- making a formal request that a copy of the fourth amended indictment be served upon the defendants in their language, because we've only received the fourth amended indictment in English, and I believe the defendants are entitled to receive it in their own language. It is the most important document in the trial, and we feel like they also, after they receive a copy in their language, they should be provided an opportunity to enter a plea to the new allegations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. I would like to ask the Prosecution on the translation of the fourth amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On that -- on that matter, I can only say that we filed the indictment signed in English, and as with the indictment -- as with the previous annexes and draft amendments, we understood that to ensure the consistency of translation, et cetera, it would be dealt within the Registry CLSS after it was filed. So we don't actually have any direct control over that translation, and I should also say we didn't request that it be urgently expedited; we presumed that it would be done as it was filed. But if it would assist in making that quicker, the Prosecution could, of course, request that. I would note that the Defence have had, in their own language, translated all the proposed wording and amendments. I -- because of the terms of the Trial Chamber's decision and specifically because the Trial Chamber requested that we be more particular with respect to dates and specific buildings in our wording, it would be the case that the defendants will not have seen that precise wording but they will have seen the wording of our proposed amendments. To be honest, I think if it's a matter of a date or that, it could be something that the counsel could confer and get instructions from their clients on as I believe they did prior to filing their response in general to the amended indictment, but that's all I can say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe the thing is to have the amended indictment read to them, then it could be simultaneously interpreted and then you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'd be happy to do that if you wish me to do it, or the registry. And the only other thing, the Prosecution would object to any formal re-entering of a plea, as Ms. Baen has suggested, because as is our position and as I understand from the Trial Chamber's decision, these are not new charges. It is not a question of a new indictment about where charges -- where a plea should be entered pursuant to the Rules and I wouldn't like that to be done in case there's any confusion as to the nature of the amendment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It's just the new particulars that will come into the fourth amended indictment. So there are no new charges at all. So it's a question of having those parts of the indictment read so that the accused can hear them in their own language or in a language they understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would Your Honour prefer me to read that out or a member of the Registry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It's usually the Registry. It's actually the additional paragraphs. If the -- yes. If the Prosecution can point them out so that -- one at a time, and then they can be read out and then interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry. Would you like me to approach the Registry and point them out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Go ahead and read them from where you are. You point out the paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly. And, Your Honour, could I just clarify? Would you like me to point out every paragraph to which there's been an amendment or only those paragraphs where the amendment relates to the destruction of religious property, or also the other harmonisation of language amendments so to speak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, only those ones with destruction of property and the other ones where we have the new capacities of the -- for criminal responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The first amendment comes in, I believe, paragraph 14(F). Do you want to read it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. 14(F).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "The destruction or wilful damage of institutions dedicated to religion, namely two Catholic churches, one in the town of Bosanski Samac about and between August 1992 and January 1993, and the other in the village of Hrvatska Tisina, about and between April 1992 and August 1992, and two mosques, one in the town of Bosanski Samac, and between August 1992 and November 1992, and the other in the town of Odzak in or about July 1992."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Paragraph 15, the operative paragraph has been slightly amended to reflect the responsibility of the defendant Blagoje Simic so the words "acting in concert with others" has been added. So it may be necessary to read that out. 15 and 15(G), which is identical to the one you've just read.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "From or on about 17 April, 1992 through to at least December 31, 1993, Blagoje Simic, both prior to and while serving as president of the Bosanski Samac --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Could you slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry. " ... of the War Presidency, acting in concert with others, planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation, or execution of the crime of persecutions as described in paragraphs 13 and 14 above through his participation in the following acts or omissions, among others: "(G) --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: (G) is exactly is the same as 14(F), isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And it runs through which paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Paragraphs 14(F), 15(G), 17(F) and 18 (G) are all identical --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Identical to what was read in paragraph 14 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 14(F), yes, so we don't need to repeat those.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly not on behalf of the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is all, isn't it? Any other --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No. The operative parts of paragraph, paragraphs 16, 17, and 18, which are very similar to 15 but involve each of the individual defendants, they have also been amended so that the same wording that was used in paragraphs -- or in 13 and 14 was reflected in 15, 16, 17, and 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the next one should be 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: 16, 17, and 18, just the operative --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Paragraphs. Okay. So we can have paragraph 16, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "From on or about 17 April 1992 through February 1993, Milan Simic, both prior to and while serving as President of the Executive Board of the Bosanski Samac assembly and as a member of the Serb Crisis Staff, acting in concert with others planned, instigated, ordered, committed or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation, or execution of the crime of persecutions as described in paragraphs 13 and 14 above, through his participation in the following acts or omissions, among others."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Proceed to paragraph 17 -- paragraph 17 and paragraph 18.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 17: "From about September 1991 to at least December 31 -- 31 December 1993, Miroslav Tadic, both prior to and while serving as a member and as chairman of the Exchange Commission and as a member of the Serb Crisis Staff, acting in concert with others planned, instigated, ordered, committed or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation or execution of the crime of persecutions as described in paragraphs 13 and 14 above through his participation in the following acts or omissions, among others." 18 --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, may I interrupt?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Because there is also an amendment to 17(E), that would be the inclusion of the wards "wanton and extensive," it may be appropriate if, since we're working our way through the indictment, if the registrar reads out 17(E) as well before proceeding to 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Yes. So 17(E).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 17(E): "The wanton and extensive destruction, plundering and looting of the property of Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims and other non-Serb civilians, including dwellings, businesses, personal property and livestock"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we go to paragraph 18.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "From about September 1991 to about 31 December 1992, Simo Zaric, both prior to and while serving in such various positions as the Assistant Commander for Intelligence, Reconnaissance, Morale and Information of the 4th Detachment, Chief of National Security Service in Bosanski Samac, Deputy to the President of the War Council for Security Matters in Odzak, and Assistant Commander of the 2nd Posavina Brigade for Morale and Information, acting in concert with others, planned, instigated, ordered, committed or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation or execution of the commission of the crimes of persecutions as described in paragraphs 13 and 14 above through his participation in the following acts or omissions, among others."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Similarly, there is the same amendment with relation to 18(F); again the addition of the words "wanton and extensive" before "destruction."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So can the registry assistant please read 18(F).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "The wanton and extensive destruction, plundering and looting of the property of Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims and other non-Serb civilians, including dwellings, businesses, personal property, and livestock."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's all, Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No. There remains the amendments to paragraphs 19 -- paragraphs 19 and 40. Those paragraphs, again, are the harmonisation of the words "acting in concert with others and together." Maybe for the completeness of the record, we should read them out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They could be.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So 19, 40 and those are the last two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Paragraphs 19 and 40.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "By these actions, Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric, acting in concert, together and with others, planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation, or execution of." 40: "From approximately 1 September 1991 through 31 December 1993, Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric, acting in concert together and with various individuals on the Serb Crisis Staff and other political, municipal and administrative bodies, the police force, and the army committed, planned, instigated, ordered or otherwise aided and abetted a campaign of persecutions for the common purpose of ridding the Bosanski Samac and Odzak municipalities of all non-Serbs, and in furtherance of the campaign, committed other serious violations of international humanitarian law directed against the Bosnian Croat, Bosnian Muslim and other non-Serb civilians residing in the Bosanski Samac and Odzak municipalities, in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Any reference to the words 'acting in concert together' shall be restricted to Count 1."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will proceed unless there are other matters. Yes, Ms. Baen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. For purposes of the record, our client, Mr. Milan Simic, does not have a copy of the indictment in front of him. So I just want that to be noted in the transcript. And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean the indictment in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. So when they're adding these paragraphs, he doesn't have this to refer to in front of him. Also for purposes of the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But he's listening to the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm sure he is, Your Honour. I'm just putting it in the transcript so that it's in the transcript that he doesn't have a copy of the indictment in front of him in his language. Then also, Rule 47(G) says if the accused doesn't understand either of the official languages of the Tribunal, then a translation of the indictment in his language shall also be prepared and shall be included as part of each certified copy of the indictment. So that's just the Rule that I'm just citing when I requested that we receive a copy of the indictment in the language of the defendant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Rule 47(G) is referring to the indictment after confirmation. That is, the initial indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour, but the indictment -- the initial indictment was the first indictment and the fourth amended indictment serves as the indictment the most important document in this trial, and it stands to reason that whichever indictment you're operating under should be translated, just as the original should be, so that the defendant can understand and see the entire charging document in his case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But the accused persons have had all these paragraphs translated. They have had the application for the amendments, the decision on the amendments, and they've been following the proceedings. So there is nothing which is strange.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're not trying to quarrel. The only thing is I feel like we're getting in a hurry here and the all that needed to happen was just to get the fourth amended indictment translated in its entirety, file it, serve a copy on the defendant, like we always do. We could have done that tonight and start tomorrow, clean, no problems. I just thought we're getting in a rush here, and I know everybody wants to move on, but I'm not quarreling with the Trial Chamber, it's just that if we feel there is some sort of issue we might need to raise for appellate purposes, it's our duty to do so. I'm not trying to offend the Trial Chamber, I'm just trying to do my job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But I think it must be understood that when we're talking about fairness to the accused or the accused following the proceedings and understanding the proceedings, there has to be a measure of reasonableness, yeah? These are matters not of technicalities. These are matters of substantive -- issues of justice. And if the Trial Chamber is satisfied that the proceedings are being followed by the accused persons, they are able to give instructions to their Defence counsels, these are not new charges, these are not new matters, they've been discussed, they've been followed by the accused persons, then the Trial Chamber is entitled to proceed. It is all right for the Defence counsel Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to place their objections on record. There's nothing wrong with that. Yes. The Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honour. Just before I ask this witness my next question, I should point out that I inadvertently referred to him by his name when I was speaking to you or making submissions to you on the issue of being able to exclude evidence from your consideration, sitting as professional Judges, and the reference to his name should be redacted or removed from the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it has been redacted, actually. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, I just wish to remind you that you are still on the solemn declaration that was taken last year and we proceed as before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Di Fazio: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before I move completely into the topic of -- of any destruction to religious institutions, there's one issue I want to clarify from the -- your earlier evidence. You mentioned that very soon after the takeover, on the 16th and 17th of April, you were attacked in Cafe AS and that you were forced to run in front of a car, with your hands in the air or trying to get your hands in the air, crying out, "Serbia, Serbia." In the car was a gentleman nicknamed Cera, whose other name is, I think, Nebojsa. Was that person a member of the 4th Detachment, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like you to turn your attention to another topic that we started to examine last time you were in this Tribunal giving evidence, and that was the destruction or damage to the mosque in Bosanski Samac. You told the Chamber how two gentleman, Perica Krstanovic, and Marinko Stefanovic came to your house, asked to borrow your Hilti drill. You said no, that you didn't have one, which was untrue, but you were concerned about it. You also said next morning that you saw that the mosque had been damaged and that you saw wires leading from the mosque into a department store and that you then went to report for your labour duties, as usual, and there you saw Kemal Mehinovic, who described what had he seen earlier that night. And I'd like you now to tell the Chamber what Kemal Mehinovic told you he had seen Perica and Marinko doing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perica Krstanovic, since he's an electrical engineer, he was connecting some wires, and Marinko was stretching the wires. Marinko is an electrician, and this is what Kemal told me as well. I didn't see this. But I did see wires crossing the asphalt, two wires. One was blue, one was white, and they were crossing -- they were stretched across the asphalt, towards the department store.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to be absolutely certain, is this the state of your evidence; the wires led from the department store to the mosque or what remained of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you're aware, did the mosque have a supply of water to it in the days when it was still existing; taps and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following the destruction of the mosque, did you do anything in respect of the water supply?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to go there, find the -- and I had to turn the water off at the main, find the water main and turn it off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzemal Kapetanovic told me that in the morning, when we reported for the work duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presumably there was some rubble or material left over from the destruction of the mosque. Can you tell the Chamber if anyone was given the task of clearing that away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the local municipal workers. They were clearing it. Because I worked in this company, and I knew the people who were clearing it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "local municipal workers," are you referring to local municipal workers who had been performing that job for a salary prior to the events -- even prior to the events of April 16 and 17 or are you talking about people who found themselves in the situation that you did, doing labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tractors -- the drivers were from Komunalo, the utility company. These were the Serbs who remained in the company. A part of the people who were assigned to work duty also went and they cleaned up this terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this destruction of the mosque commented upon in the local Serb radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear it, the commentary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who commented and what was said about the destruction of the mosque in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: A comment was read by Mira Lujic, anchor on the local radio, and she said that the Ustashas had blown up the mosque. Later, a day or two afterwards, it was said that a rocket from the Croat side had hit the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you now to turn your attention to the mosque in Odzak. You gave evidence in December that you spent quite some time in Odzak, performing these labour duties that you've described in detail. Can you tell us if the mosque in Odzak was damaged at all in the time that you were doing labour duties in Odzak or whether it was damaged earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day before I left for Odzak, the mosque was blown up. So I wasn't there that day when the mosque was blown up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber if the destruction of the mosque in Odzak was commented upon in the radio, and if so, who said -- who commented upon it and what was said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing, that Ustashas had done that, Ustasha -- Ustasha scouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you see it with your own eyes that the mosque had in fact been destroyed or damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a Catholic church in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first started -- when you first started doing your labour duties in Odzak, was it standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it ever subsequently damaged or destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the 17th of August, it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I ask you to continue with this narrative, can you tell the Chamber, how many Catholic churches were there in Bosanski Samac and in Odzak and how many mosques were there in Bosanski Samac and Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one mosque in Bosanski Samac. And in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, there was one Catholic church in Samac, there was one in Hrvatska Tisina, one in Hasici, in Korenica, in Prud. Also in the Odzak municipality, it's not mentioned, but there was one in Gornja Dubica, Balic. All those churches were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber if the Croat villages in the municipality of Bosanski Samac had only one church normally in the little village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Hasici, I think. No, there were churches. There was a monastery in Kornica. That's where the nuns were. This was knocked down, it was burned. There was one church in Hrvatska Tisina. The church was not knocked down in Hasici, only the crosses were changed, but the church itself remained standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, recalling that the fourth amended indictment is restricting us -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'm mindful of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: -- to two Catholic churches, et cetera, we seem to be going broader than this. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand that, if Your Honours please. I was merely trying to establish the number of mosques and churches in Bosanski Samac and in Odzak and the fact whether other Croat villages normally had only one particular church. Now, that's relevant, I think, to Tisina and to Odzak and -- Odzak and Bosanski Samac. I wasn't trying to elicit -- that wasn't my objective in asking those questions but merely to establish how many -- numbers of churches in those -- and mosques in those places. It will go a long way to any complaints by the Defence to say that they -- and addresses any complaint by the Defence that -- of uncertainty if there's only one mosque and only one Catholic church in Odzak and only one mosque and only one Catholic church in Bosanski Samac. So that was the objective of my question, not to elicit evidence of widespread damage and go further than I have been permitted to by the Chamber. But now that I see Your Honour's comment, it brings us fairly and squarely to this issue of the Catholic church in -- in Odzak. I think the amendments that you have permitted only go to the Catholic church in Bosanski Samac and Tisina. My submission is that, notwithstanding the amendments that the Chamber has permitted the Prosecution to make, it still remains relevant evidence of the -- under Rule 93, for a start, and also given the -- given the wording of the Chamber's decision on -- on the amendments. The Chamber said, in dealing with amendments concerning destruction or wilful damage of institutions dedicated to religion --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down. MR. DI FAZIO: I apologise. The Chamber said, in dealing with amendments concerning destruction or wilful damage of institutions to religion, and I refer in particular to paragraph 4 on page 2 of the decision: "The Trial Chamber arrives at this conclusion after carefully considering the arguments of both parties and particularly the argument of the Prosecution that the destruction or wilful damage of institutions dedicated to religion are charged as part of the discriminatory attack against non-Serbs, the institutions being part of their religious identity under persecution as a crime against humanity." Now, I'm mindful of my limitations as set out in the amendments that have been permitted by the Chamber. It's under that heading that I would seek to introduce this evidence of damage to the Catholic church in Odzak, notwithstanding the limitations of the permitted amendments. If you think that that's not to be permitted, then there can be no justification for my continuing this line of questioning in respect of the Catholic church in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I think perhaps you may just want to confine yourself with the amendment, the limitation contained therein. All right? MR. DI FAZIO: As Your Honours please. May I just have a moment to confer with my colleagues, because that may rapidly bring me to a close in my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Witness, if there was a Catholic church in the village of Tisina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the months following April 16th and prior to your arrest, did you ever have an opportunity of going to Tisina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the Catholic church there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea as to who damaged it or how it was damaged or when it was damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but when we went to Hasici, we passed through that area because the church is right by the road, and the tower, the spire had been blown up. And a building next to the church was also destroyed and plundered. It was sometime in June, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it -- the damage or destruction of that particular church reported upon in the -- by the radio, as the mosques had been reported upon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly. There were some comments on the radio, but the main comment was that the Mujahedin from Gradacac did that, that they had come and blown up the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on Bosanski Samac radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the same lady who you mentioned had commented on the destruction of the mosques in --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown -- can the witness be shown Exhibit P14, which are the photographs, and in particular, photographs number 24 to 26. Perhaps it's P14A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it's P14A. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Perhaps if we could start, just quickly, with P14A, photograph number 24. I don't know, it might be better for the defendants, I think, if it was placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The particular photograph which you want to discuss with the witness should be on the ELMO. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Di Fazio, if the usher could make sure that we don't see the list with the numbers and the names of the photographs, which we did get a brief glance of a few moments ago. MR. DI FAZIO: Oh, yes. Yes. Yes. Are you asking that they be removed from the view of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. It just appeared briefly on the screen. MR. DI FAZIO: It's been attended to. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, what's that a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Catholic church in Hrvatska Tisina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw it, was it in that state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And please place photograph number 25 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber what that photograph shows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the interior of the church in Hrvatska Tisina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And now, Mr. Usher, could you please place photograph number 26.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, there are two buildings you can see there. I don't think anyone's going to object if I suggest that the one on the right is the church you've just been talking about. What about the other building in the background and on the left? Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another church building where the priest by the name of Zuparic lived. Later on, Lugar had his headquarters in this house where the priest used to live.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When? When did he have his headquarters there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe May, June 1992. He was there with his ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think you finished your answer. He was there with his what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: With his troops, the mercenaries from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a priest who used to reside there. What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also imprisoned in the TO building in Bosanski Samac. He was exchanged, and I don't know his present whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just repeat again the surname of the priest.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zuparic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I have just a moment to confer with my colleagues, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Witness, did you just try to say something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I just remembered, actually, his name is Puskaric. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know whether I should start with my cross-examination, in light of the break. Could you perhaps tell me now when you intend to have a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Maybe we can have a break and continue our proceedings at 1615 hours. Then the cross-examination can start then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: May I just raise one very brief matter before my friends cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And that is the timing of witnesses. As you know, it is proposed after this witness is called that the next witness be the gentleman who needs to be cross-examined who gave his evidence last year, Mr. Dagovic, and he's available and will be called. The question is precisely when. My learned friends have apparently indicated to my colleague Ms. Reidy that their estimate for cross-examination of this witness is 4 hours. That will take us through today and into tomorrow, of course, but the question is how far -- much of tomorrow, and the other witness is waiting in the wings, ready for his cross-examination, and therefore has to be arranged. I, with all due respect to my learned friends and I think four hours is probably fairly optimistic on their part, that we will probably go at least all of tomorrow if not very close to the end of tomorrow. Of course, they know their case better, but even with the best of intentions, estimates are usually underestimates rather than overestimates. Would the Chamber be minded to grant us permission to arrange him for Wednesday morning rather than tomorrow afternoon? He doesn't have to be flown in, he's driving in from somewhere, and it means something to him to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: -- to have the day, the extra day tomorrow. What I'm worried about is that we finish slightly early and we haven't got a witness waiting in the wings. If that were to arise, would the Chamber give us an adjournment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We can agree that he can drive in on Wednesday morning. MR. DI FAZIO: Wednesday morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir. My name is Novak Lukic. I'm an attorney, and I'm the Defence counsel for Mr. Miroslav Tadic, and I will be asking you some questions in my capacity. Before I begin, I would just like to let you know two things. First of all, it's been a month and a half since our last meeting here in this courtroom. During my cross-examination, I will probably have to remind you of some of the sentences you have uttered, although I assumed you remember quite clearly all the things that you said during your testimony a month and a half ago. The second thing I would like to note is I would like to make this -- the proceedings more economical in light of the duration of all the testimonies. I would like to ask you if you could keep your answers as short and as simple as possible. I will try to phrase my questions in such a way that you can answer with yes or no or I don't know or I do not remember. After all, you have been able to answer such -- in such a way to some of the questions asked by my learned colleague from the Prosecution, and I will try to follow his example. First of all, I would like to remind you of what you have said and ask you the following question in this respect: You stated that you had -- that you were a member of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand, you were a member of this party for just a few months.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The microphone when asking your question, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were some disagreements with the persons who were active members of the party. You quoted that as the reason why you left the SDA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I please ask you to wait for the interpretation of my question and then give your answer, for the purpose of interpretation. Can we agree that you were in conflict with Mr. Safet Hadzialijagic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please wait for the interpretation, because we cannot hear his answer clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us proceed slowly. I will try to use the same tactics used by my colleague Mr. Pantelic. When you hear my question, count to five and then answer, because in that way we will avoid the problem with the interpretation. I will repeat my question. Were you in conflict with Mr. Safet Hadzialijagic, nicknamed Coner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in conflict with him also while you were a member of the League of Communists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe I can explain to the witness that if you're looking at the screen, you will notice that when a sentence is completed, there is a black indicator at the end of it and it will flash about three, four times without moving further. That means the interpretation is completed for our purposes. So just observe that and you can give your answer, because the interpreters have to complete the question of counsel before they can interpret your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, Mr. Lukic, I wonder whether you could clarify from the witness. If you look at line 24, the answer to your question as to being in conflict with Mr. Safet Hadzialijagic is, "No," and then you ask the same question, line -- page 34, line 7, and the answer on line 9 is, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I noted this as an error in interpretation, and that is why I repeated the question. The answer given by the witness the first time was, "Yes," but the transcript read, "No," and that is why I repeated the question. I think that now we have cleared this whole issue up. He was in indeed conflict, had a dispute with Mr. Safet Hadzialijagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After doing your national service - you already described this to the Prosecutor - were you in any kind of reserve force? And if yes, where, in which arm of the service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while I was in the reserve force of the police. As for the arm, I don't know. Just the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the reserve force of the police until the outbreak of the conflict or did you change your assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I changed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have military exercises?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you issued with any kind of weapon as a member of the reserves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can agree that you only knew where your order of war timetable was, but you weren't assigned to any kind of unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had lectures often. This is what it really was all about mostly, at the old hotel in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the army you were trained how to handle weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also described to us the day when weapons were issued in the TO building. So we -- I would like to clarify some facts regarding this event. First of all, I'm interested in whether you found out from somebody that these weapons were being issued or distributed at the TO or you saw people on the street who were carrying weapons and then you went to the TO. Could you please just clarify this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a couple of people carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask them where they got the weapons from, why they were carrying these weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I think I asked a person. His last names is Coralic. His nickname is Dubcek or Ciko. And He told me that the TO, the Territorial Defence in Samac, was distributing weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time did you know that a new Territorial Defence was formed in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find out that day that the chief of the TO headquarters was Marko Bozanic and that the commander was Alija Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about Alija before. I knew Marko personally, and I happened to see him there at the HQ that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more clarification, if you would. Could you precisely tell us whether you saw Milos Bogdanovic in the courtyard of the TO building on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that you saw that only Muslims and Croats were issued with weapons. This is what you said. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could anybody receive a rifle who happened to come to the TO building courtyard at that time and ask for a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who decided about who could be issued with a weapon and who could not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who made that decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a list of people who were supposed to be issued with weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were offered a rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to remind you of your statement which you gave in the month of December. You stated literally that it seemed to you that this was a kind of funny business going on and this is why you decided to leave, and you were not on the list to receive a weapon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've stated a little while ago that I did not see this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask for a weapon at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, and I'm sure I wouldn't have received one either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you clarify for me, please, what you meant when you said that it seemed to you that there was some funny business going on there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was watching as they were distributing the weapons at the HQ. The door was open. When I turned to the other side, towards the building of the police station, I could see that Serb police officers were looking out of the windows from that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to you, could those police officers clearly see who was bringing out rifles from the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that that evening, your brother [redacted] came to ask you for a rifle, even though you'd never had one before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask him why he was asking you for a rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did ask him, and he told me, "If you do have one, give it to me." And he told me also to stay in the house, not to go out and not to open the door. Since it was possible to buy an illegal weapon at that time, perhaps he thought that I had bought a rifle somewhere, and this is probably why he came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to move to another topic now. You described your forced labour and your trench digging. You stated that you were summoned for work duty in the second half of May, that you received the summons then on the 16th or the 17th of May.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I hear you properly, that you stated that already the next day you had gone out to dig trenches in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like you to clarify some things about the area we're talking about. You also indicated some of these places on the map. The line of separation at that time was between -- the River Bosna at that time was the line of separation between the HVO and the units of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to this line of separation, did something change after Odzak was taken over by the VRS in July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the usher to place the map P9 on the ELMO so that we could clarify some points regarding the location of Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point out for us the village of Zasavica on this map, please. Once again, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be easier to look on the map itself rather than on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also pointed out the line of trenches that you had made during the months of May and June, i.e., in the month of May when the work duty began. Could you please show that to us once more.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not able to hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters say they can't hear what the witness is saying. I wonder if he can be assisted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the village of Zasavica up to the Bosna River, the line went. This is where Prudine are, then it went towards Pisari, even though they're not indicated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, you've already marked that. When did the Muslims swim across the Sava River in large numbers? When was this? In which month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the 15th of July. Mid-July, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, as you stated, their families were detained in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. village of Zasavica as a consequence of that act.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the fall of Odzak, after Odzak was taken over by the Serb authorities, that's when it happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that at the time when the families of these people were taken to Zasavica, the River Bosna was not the separation line between the warring parties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was digging trenches in the month of May, and I agree that at that time when there was this major escape attempt, the River Bosna was not the separation between the sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that, at that time, the line of the front ran along the River Sava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's where it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how far, approximately, is Zasavica from the River Sava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean if we go along the River Bosna or if we go along the road?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what is the shortest distance between Zasavica and the River Sava, according to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's perhaps about eight kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the town Samac is on the bank of the River Sava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the village -- that the village of Zasavica was ever shelled from the direction of the Sava River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As opposed to Samac, which was frequently shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We won't need map P9 any more, thank you. Actually, I would just like it to stay on the ELMO for just one more question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the map, you can see the town of Samac. You can see it very well. But perhaps you could indicate where the old-age pensioners' hall was where you had to report for work duty. If you can indicate where it was, approximately. Was it in the town itself? Was it in the centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This building had a ground floor and a first floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had apartments upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the offices for the work duty were in the basement, on the ground floor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is where people reported for their work duty assignments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that you frequently went upstairs where your brother Ismet worked.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can agree, can we not, that on the first floor, the upstairs of the building, there were the premises of the local Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Red Cross flag was flying on that building, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean; "No, it was not there," or, "No, I don't remember"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I remember there was the employment office there. I do not recall any flag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was in charge of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Sveto Vasovic, the teacher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the name Milorad Mihajlovic ring any bells?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he work for the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in fact the manager for the Red Cross in Samac? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of Anka Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name Zeljko Volasevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I think that Zeljko did not work for the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Anka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anka did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who wanted to being exchanged, did they go to the premises of the Red Cross to sign up for it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they went to the premises where my brother and Mr. Miroslav Tadic were, but we're talking about a different premises. That's not the Red Cross building. That was, in fact, a separate room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have to agree. In addition to the Red Cross, was there also the civilian protection there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the local commune council where Zeljko Volasevic used to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the civilian protection headquarters? If you don't know, just say -- just say so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the civilian protection is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Miroslav Tadic was the commander of the civilian protection headquarters or staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that if somebody wanted to be exchanged, that the other side had to give its approval; the other side, the receiving side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I merely asked about your knowledge of this fact, whether it was necessary to receive approval from the receiving side for any exchange.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not want to answer that question because the question itself is not correct. They took people to be exchanged, those who wanted to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that if somebody wanted to be exchanged and go to the Republic of Croatia, that they needed a letter of guarantee from a person inviting this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. Who would give you such a letter of guarantee that they were willing to receive you? That's also not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you to assess my question but to give me an answer. Do you know of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your brother worked in the premises where Miroslav Tadic was the manager.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this his work duty assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in a military uniform. I would say that this was his work duty assignment. He was paid as a soldier of the Republika Srpska army, and whether this was in fact work duty, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you some questions that pertain to the proceedings conducted against you. My learned colleague from the Prosecution wanted to ask you some questions regarding this event, but we did not -- we were not able to get any answers. I just want to ask you, is your eyesight better now than it was in December?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I may want to ask you to read some things. In the course of the examination-in-chief, you said you were arrested in September [Realtime transcript read in error "December"] 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were questioned by Inspector Milos Savic after perhaps some ten days.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm little bit concerned, and I don't want to interrupt unduly, but I'm a bit concerned about what was put to the witness about the date. It says December 1992. I don't have it at my fingertips, but my memory tells me that the arrest was earlier than what this witness said, and I think my colleague Mr. Weiner agrees with me. I wonder if Mr. Lukic can specify the page or if he has direct knowledge of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: About the date of arrest for the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. On the translation here, it says December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that on the transcript. MR. DI FAZIO: My memory tells me that his evidence was that he was arrested much earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question that I asked was September, and the witness heard me and answered and confirmed it. So we're talking about September 1992. MR. DI FAZIO: Fine. It's been clarified. It's just a mistake in interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
