utterances.text: We have a problem because this is the second time the interpretation seems not to be correct. So the month is September. Let the witness confirm that if the witness can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In December I was taken from Samac to Batkovici and that is why the month of December is mentioned at all, but I was arrested in September 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I even quoted the exact reference; page 5223 of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated that you couldn't remember whether you signed any written statements.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated that you were questioned only about the fact whether you belonged to the scout unit, Alija's scouts, as you explained to us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Savic did not ask any other questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no other questions. That was the only thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also answered to my colleague from the Prosecution that there was no mention of Stevo Arandjic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Stevo Arandjic was not mentioned at all on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about the incident involving Stevo Arandjic, nothing was said about that either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing was said about that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now go into private session or closed session, because I would now like to introduce a document where the witness's name is mentioned, and I would like to have a part of this document read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were exchanged in June 1994.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, there's just one particular matter that I need -- I think should be clarified for the benefit of the Chamber. It's an earlier question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Question: "I assume that the money was taken away from all persons who were imprisoned at Batkovic," and the -- what the question -- and the answer was: "Yes." What that leaves unanswered is whether the money was taken at Batkovic or at some other place or only taken from the people who went to Batkovic. So perhaps that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure counsel can deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just clarify this issue. When you were searched, as you entered Batkovic, by the officials there, any money that was found was seized on the spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that now it has been clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that at that time in June 1994, 18 persons were exchanged, persons who were with you in Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those your fellow citizens from Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were six of us from Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any of the names, or perhaps all of the names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Husein Arapovic, Zlatko Dubric, Esad Dzakic, and Mirsad Srna, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you found out the day before the exchange that you were going to be exchanged. Do you know who organised the exchange? Were you taken to the exchange by the army of the Republika Srpska? Were they uniformed persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were people in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there uniformed persons from the B and H army during the exchange? Were they present also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to see the people who were being exchanged for you? Did you see people coming from the opposite side at the place where the exchange took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated that you gave a statement afterwards. Do you remember to whom you gave that first statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the police in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were representatives of the International Red Cross present during that -- on that occasion, or representatives of the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were uniformed persons from one and from the other side there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miroslav Tadic was not present at that exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you were exchanged, as far as I was able to figure out, you had served about two years of that sentence by the military court. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were still serving that sentence when you went to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A 12-year sentence in prison, according to the judgement of the military court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that, in response to a question by the Prosecutor about your exchange, which you gave in December of last year on page 5252, when the Prosecutor asked whether there were any soldiers or military persons present at that exchange, you had responded, "No."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a military escort on both sides, because we were treated as members of the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I'm interested in. Were you treated as war -- prisoners of war by the persons who took you for the exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the documents, that is how we were treated. Civilians were given -- were exchanged for regular army members in these exchanges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the -- and the judgement by the -- did you have this sentence, the judgement by the military court which sentenced you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were -- the 37 from us from Samac, we were sentenced. So we were exchanged for the members of the army who had been captured on the lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I concluded rightly, during the exchange, the people who were exchanged from the other side were military persons, persons from the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I have a question for yourself. If this witnesses and others like him in a similar situation were classified as prisoners of war, on what basis were they being prosecuted? They would have been subjected to the protections of international humanitarian law, the Geneva Conventions 1949. So these prosecutions would hardly have been legal and there would also be questions as to the -- obviously the beatings would again violate the legal obligations both under conventional international law and customary international law and arguably also jus cogens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood your question very well, Judge Williams, but I am defending Miroslav Tadic here, who was not a party to the decision of the military court. He did not participate in the exchange of this witness. So I'm trying, through the procedure which was conducted - and this Court will decide about the legality of that procedure - I am trying -- I would like to show through that procedure what the -- what the activities or the procedure of Miroslav Tadic was in the committee for the exchange, because earlier with previous witnesses, I provided documents about who it is who approves military exchanges, if you remember. And I provided this document as the main headquarters of Republika Srpska, the corps command, if we're talking about exchange. So in this sense, the situation relating to the legality or the justice of his procedure, a military trial is in somebody else's jurisdiction. I'm asking these questions in order to clarify the place and the role of my defendant in the procedure of the exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But I think your question was, and which I also don't quite understand, the question you put to him was: "You were treated as war prisoners by the persons who took you for the exchange." What does that mean? What persons? What persons are you talking about who took him for the exchange? Who are these persons, the authorities?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there was a civilian and a military committee for exchange as part of the authorities of Republika Srpska. Military prisoners of war who were treated as such by the authorities of Republika Srpska, based on some legal documents, were exchanged through military commissions; and civilians who were treated by those commissions as civilians were exchanged through civilian committees. During the year 1993, these committees became mixed, and they always worked jointly. And we will present evidence of this during the trial. But my questions was, the people who took him for an exchange, were they uniformed persons? This is what I wanted to find out from the witness. These were people who took him to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Judge Singh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Do you know who took him to be exchanged to the authorities? If you know, you should put that to him. I assume you know by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must disappoint you. I only know about exchanges in which my client participated, and I can assume who it was who took him to the -- to be exchanged. But the exchanges in which my client Tadic participated, I know about those specifically. But I assume it was somebody from the military structure from the camp, or he was simply taken there by people from the military command. Perhaps we can clarify this if the witness knows this in regard to his exchange.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when the list was read by a civilian, the list was read to us by a civilian person, his name is Vojkan Djurkovic. He read a list to us in the camp. He was the president of the committee in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is 6.00. I have one more topic besides the topic which was postponed. So perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can adjourn and continue tomorrow afternoon at 1415. I see Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Your Honours. I was informed during the break from my client that he doesn't feel very well at all, and he is willing to rest tomorrow, and I just wanted to inform the Trial Chamber that he's waiving his right of appearance for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So he can rest in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.
